From: Phil Glover, BIRMINGHAM

I am writing to say how good I
think Bob Wilkinson's 'OUTWRITE'
program is. I was lucky to buy a
pre-production copy at the All
Format Computer Fair,Birmingham.

As a Tasword fan I may wait and
hope for a 'real' Sam version of
Tasword though 'OUTWRITE' seems
to be an excellent program and
is very easy to use. I'm looking
forward to receiving the manual
to see if I have yet to discover
more about it. I am particularly
pleased to find that the program
LOADs Tasword II files from both
Plus D disks and Sam disks and
was very pleased to find that
there was no keyboard bounce!

'OUTWRITE' deserves to be a very
popular program.I hope it proves
a great success for you all.I'll
be on the lookout amongst the
Sam and Spectrum publications to
see what sort of reviews
'OUTWRITE'gets and if any review
is poor that critic will
certainly lose respect from me!

If Tasman decide to resume their
Sam Tasword program they'll have
to work hard to surpass the
standard set by Bob Wilkinson.
They may be good at mail-merge,
search, find and replace, and
other facilities but the main
strength of a word processor is
the ease of typing and the gen-
eral ease of use of the main
functions. OUTWRITE has achieved
that very well indeed.

Congratulations to all involved
with 'OUTWRITE' and continued
sucess with Outlet. As long as
you keep turning out such a good
magazine, I'll keep subscribing!

        Yours sincerely,

           Phil Glover






Many thanks, Phil and you will
have received the manual and the
free upgrade to version 1.1
since writing your letter.

                        - Brian

From: Cliff Jackson,SOUTHAMPTON


Dear Ron and Brian,

Re: Spectrum 128K sound.

I read somewhere a long time ago
that the 128's sound output from
the AY-3-8912 Programmable Sound
Generator (to use the official
description) is available on the
"Ear" socket and is therefore
available for external
amplification, recording etc.

Long before I bought my 128K, I
built a plug-in board with an AY
sound chip which worked happily
on my 48K+ using its on-board
amplifier.

When the 128K took pride of
place on my desk I found Uncle
Clive had chosen different Port
addresses but this was overcome
by altering my (own) software.

About the same time I built a
Save/Load switch to avoid
unplugging leads. This was
retired when I got a Datacorder
from W.H. Smith which has a
"Spectrum" switch removing the
need to disconnect leads.

When the 128K arrived the switch
was modified to act as a
"Computer Select" box to enable
the Data Corder to be used with
either computer at the flick of
one switch - and is still in use
in that form.

I was disappointed by the frying
bacon background noises from the
loudspeaker which I initially
blamed on the T/V, a 14" b/w
portable but later I found that
a colour set of different make
was exactly the same.I had a car
loud-speaker in a plastic
moulding (for rear shelf) and
into the limited space available
fitted a strip of Vero-board
onto which I had built a small
audio amplifier.

This was inserted between the
Datacorder and the switch box so
that it intercepted signals in
both directions. Initially the
board was powered by a PP9
battery but, as I frequently
forgot to switch it off, I later

connected the 9-volt unregulated
output from the Sinclair Power
Supply which then powered the
board through a regulator which
I added, before going on to the
128K.

One of my first mods. to the 48K
had been to fit a small switch
in the internal "loudspeaker"
lead so that late-night or
early-morning sessions did not
disturb the family but I now had
a variable-volume sound output
for either computer selected by
the "tape" switch.

This has been in daily use for
over two years and happily
produces all the Beeps which my
programs use to wake me up when

I try to do something stupid
like loading Tasword +2 in 48K
mode.

However, when I ran David
Wornham's "Reel" from Issue #040
I noticed that the sound became
barely audible in alternate
"verses". Eventually I realised
that it is the 3-channel sound
from the AY chip which is at a
much lower volume than the Beep
output, both of which are taken
from the "ear" line.

I now have a monitor with sound
but there is no sound output
from the 128's 8-pin DIN socket
so the only way to get sound
from the modem's integral
speaker is via the "ear" line.

This I have linked to the audio
line of the Scart socket on the
monitor and thus get exactly the
same results as from my own
amplifier and without the
unwanted background noise but it
came as a surprise to find that
the sound-chip output was so
feeble when the Beeps are super.


Does anyone out there know if
this is normal or have I got a
fault on my 128K?. Alternatively
is there a sound output from the
chip at the expansion port or
can the audio be separated from
the video on the "T/V" output?
Presumably the latter would
suffer from the frying bacon
sounds which the T/V produced.

Using sound-chip output only, I
tried turning up the volume
which was OK until either a key
was pressed or a Beep type
output encountered, and then the
ear-drums had a hard time.

Another hardware project was a
combined "switchable" joystick
port and external key-board
port.This was based on Adrian
Dickens' designs in his
excellent Manual 'Spectrum
Hardware'. The switching was
provided by five pairs of DIL 8
pole, 1-way slider switches
which enabled any single-press
key to be allocated to the
joystick which I also made. It
differs from the standard stick
by having 10 conductors in the


lead (rather than the standard
six) to give individual ground
connections (not "commoned").
The circuit scans Port address
254 and reads IN 31,the Kempston
standard. This works fine on the
48K machine but will not work on
the 128K/Disciple combination.
Initially I thought it was just
the change of port addresses as
the results are different if you
enter:
    10 PRINT AT 0,0;IN 31;"  " :
       GO TO 10
the joystick produces:
             48K     128K
  No press    0      224
  Right       1      225
  Left        2      226
  Down        4      228
  Up          8      232
  Fire       16      240

Any combination may be used thus
enabling diagonal movements - it
does not lock like the key-board
does when 2 or more keys are
pressed simultaneously.

I suspect commercial software
which does not insist on 48K
mode must allow for differing
inputs. The 128 results however
are not merely 224 higher.If you
try:
    10 CLS
    20 PRINT IN 31;" ": GOTO 20
you will find that occasionally
the number returned is 32 lower
than the rest e.g. 224 comes out
as 192 etc. This is easy enough
to mask but the Disciple does
not like this add-on although it
works OK with a PIO chip I also
added to the board.

I recall reading (in the distant
days when Your Computer was a
treasure house for serious
users) of a "bit 6 problem" but
at the time I didn't know a bit
from a saddle so the signific-
ance was lost on me but I
suspect that bit 6 of port 31
must "flip" occasionally.

Hardware is not difficult but
needs the background information
which was so well provided by
Adrian Dickens for the 48K user.
There must be someone out there
who has technical information
like Port Addresses for the
later machines and Disciple, and
can point us would-be hardware
constructors in the right
direction. How about a series on
hardware?

Finally to Ron and Brian thanks
once again for your splendid
efforts. Your support both moral
and practical to those with
problems is highly commendable.
The courtesy and efficiency with
which contributions are handled
earns much respect and the
content of Outlet gets better
all the time. With best wishes.

          Cliff Jackson

Brian Cavers to Cliff Jackson

Thanks Cliff. Not being a hard-
ware expert I can only add one
or two things to that and leave
the rest to input from others.

According to page 139 of the +3
manual if each of the three
channels of the sound chip are
played at maximum volume then
the total output is equal to
that from BEEP.Therefore a piece
of music using perhaps just two
channels or even all three where
they are not all playing exactly
the same note in unison will be
at a lower volume than BEEP. In
practice this doesn't appear so
noticeable as your set up seems
to be - subjective perhaps?

Regarding port reading variation
with a Disciple attached, I had
trouble with IN 32766 which I
use to test for a keypress of
the symbol key in CATLOADER
(OUTLET 44). It worked fine on
my machine with a consistent
value but Ron's machine fluctu-
ated between two values! He got
round it with a slight change to
the BASIC but it was baffling
for a while!

The only titbit of info I have
is IN 187 pages IN the Disciple
ROM while OUT 187 pages it out!

                        - Brian

From: Frank Lambert, HORNCHURCH

Re: Malcolm Goodman's comment on
labelling, can I refer you to a
competitor's labelling - namely
"FRED"? I store the same way as
Malcolm and believe that your
labelling is correct as it
allows the legend to be read on
offering the disk to the drive -
but although it means a larger
label, the edge legend is
invaluable in the storage box.

'SAMCLASS' re: your request for
comments on BASIC. I think a
series on differences between
Spectrum and Sam BASICs would be
particularly useful if it could
be done. I find the 'User Guide'
quite inadequate. What would
really be useful would be for

someone 'out there' to reset
"The Century Computer Programm-
ing Course" How about it Messrs.
MORSE, ADAMSON et al?

DISPLAY SYSTEMS:I realise now as
a matter of urgency that I have
to invest in a monitor to get
the best from SAM. From comments
in the magazine it seems to be a
veritable "minefield" to get the
correct type - blank screens,
through colour incompatability,
linear RGB, CGA/EGA/VGA/MDA -
whatever they might mean, even
sound availability. I was, how-
ever, impressed by Tony Blythe's
comments on the Phillips CM8833
but can you recommend any review
articles or sources of compar-
ative information?

When sending control characters
to the printer I've run into a
strange problem I'm totally
unable to understand. Starting
with your line:-
 1410 LPRINT CHR$ O;CHR$ VAL
      "27"; "@"; CHR$ VAL
      "27";"1";CHR$ O8=RETURN
a) This works perfectly satis-
   factorily.
b) If I replace the 8 in CHR$ O8
   with n (n = 1,2,3,4,5,6,7, or
   9) so the left margin is set
   to "n"; I get an error code
   on "setting":-
   "2 n not found, 1410:1"
c) If the "n" is returned to 8
   then the line works again.
d) If,however,O8 is replaced by
   0n or n the line is accepted
   and sets the margin to n.

e) In fact O8 (your program) can
   be replaced by o(alphabetic)
   8 or 08.

f) On inspecting the rest of the
   program O and 0 seem to print
   on the screen interchangeably
   -am I missing something obvi-
   ous?Can Brian please explain?

What is the purpose of CHR$ O in
LPRINT CHR$ O? I find O can be
replaced by O(alphabetic) or 0 -
and indeed CHR$O can be deleted
altogether without causing any
difference in the execution.
I still don't know how you
manage it, but the magazine gets
better and better!

             Frank Lambert

Brian Cavers to Frank Lambert

We use a small disc label as the
extra time and labour involved
in sticking full-size,wrap-round
labels onto hundreds of discs is
considerable. A small label need
only be approximately central
whereas the full label looks bad
if it's even slightly out of
line and, of course is MUCH more
fiddly to stick on the discs. In
my own system I always use the
full labels. I write on front,
back and edge and store them so
I can read the spines. I put the
labels on upside down with the
colour area at the top as the
spines are difficult to read
with dark colours like red or
purple!

I, too, think a simple class on
SAM BASIC would be a good idea -
to supplement the machine code
of SAMCLASS.If anyone would like
to write an article or series of
articles for us please let me
know - remember, we do pay a
modest amount for contributions!
I'd like to do it myself but it
is hopeless trying to find time
- can you believe I'm typing
this at 4.45 am and I finished
work last night at gone 11.00pm?
Mind you, that's unusual.I often
finish work by 9.00pm and have a
lie in until 6.00 am the next
day! You can appreciate why an
hour saved on labelling is so
precious! Try timing yourself
with a stop watch sticking both
types of label!

I can't refer you to any review
articles on monitors other than
comments in these pages. I'm not
sure how relevant a review in
say, a PC magazine would be any-
way. Comments from readers, good
or bad, on the monitor they use
are always welcome. I doubt that
one could better what we have
heard about the Philips one.

My own one is a JVC TM 150 PSN-K
and it gives a good sharp image.
There is slight ghosting (which
doesn't bother me much) but I
don't know whether this is due
to my individual SAM or SAMs in
general. Brightness has to be up
FULL - a bad sign - and the same
comments apply. The screen is
also VERY reflective in a sunny
room!

The O8 in line 1410 is a numeric
variable consisting of a capital
letter "O" and the digit 8 -just
like say, x2. The variable is
set up by a READ statement at
line 9930 - the DATA being at
line 30 and has a value of 8. It
is used instead of using just an
8 to save memory because numbers
have 6 extra hidden bytes each
time they appear in a listing
and the value 8 occurs several
times in the CONTENTS BASIC. I
also use O for zero and I for 1.
In other programs I often set up
O,I,O2,O3 etc. up to I0,I1,I2
and so on. If you substitute,say
O5 for the O8 in line 1410 then
no such variable as O5 exists in
the CONTENTS BASIC so it won't
work!                - Brian

From Malcolm Perry


Re: David Smith (Wolverhampton)
Query: DATEL DOS.

Firstly I must stress I do not
know what DOS DATEL are sending
out with their +Ds since taking
over from MGT therefore these
notes are based on pre-DATEL
information. Secondly, unless
DATEL have altered things, 3C is
more related to the DISCIPLE.
So, bearing this uncertainty in
mind, here goes.

Disciple started life,I believe,
with a V2 ROM and associated DOS
and was upgraded to V3 ROM and
3a DOS(review #1 Format AUG.87)

V3a dos was then progressivly
upgraded to B,C then to D Each
change was to overcome various
bugs or problems that were found
from use. (in fact c to d was,it
seems, more to add in something
that got left out of the C
update). Without going into
detail the latest version is
more reliable with twin drives
and handling OPENTYPE files.
There was also a mod to prevent
a hangup associated with BOOT if
printer not on, A 128 mod to
stop dropping back to 48k after
a file COPY and so on.

The +D has 2 ROM versions 1 and
1A.The latter overcomes problems
of some drives not finding track
0.(I believe). Therefore GDOS1
was changed to GDOS2 for ROM1a.

However, the two DOS's are
basically the same. Both these
were updated to 1a/2a again to
overcome problems with OPENTYPE
files, to work with the full
screen editor in 128k mode and
to prevent dropping back to 48k
after a SAVE TO.

There were some v3 +D dos's (I
had one) which I understand was
a part conversion similar to the
'a update but not exactly the
same (and caused me problems).

Is it worth upgrading? The obvi-
ous answer is yes for the added
reliability, removal of bugs and
some snags. Also, I have found
some programs will only work on
the latest version of DOS.(Some
state this).

There again, if you have not
experienced any problems in the
past then probably it's not
worth spending to get the later
version. The updates do not
actually provide extended
functions or facilities unless
you update to UNI-DOS or BETADOS
which is another matter.

Assuming DATEL have not altered
things then 2A is the latest for
the +D which D. Smith has.

For those interested,the follow-
ing FORMATs cover the updates
(the code to D.I.Y.) Disciple,
#3 (a-b) #10(b-c) #11(c-d) +D
#11 (1/2 to 1a/2a). Format also
sell both the latest DOS (to
members).

UNI-DOS update. (Disciple / +D)
Since my review (OUTLET 45), I
have used quite a lot more
programs and sub routines mostly
from various OUTLETS all without
problems(The KEYWORD incompati-
bility was covered in review and
resolved). I consider the
compatibility is a lot better
than I first thought with GDOS.
The colour dump problem has also
been resolved with a small mod
to the code. (This mod actually
appeared in FORMAT V3 #3 for a
different purpose and was to
make the dump compatible with
interfaces other than Disciple).
I am certainly happy and the
advantages outweigh the few
disadvantages.I have also since
found the author of Uni-Dos to
be helpful.

Time has only strengthened my
opinions in favour. Therefore,
providing one is prepared to
accept some incompatibilities
mainly where the program
actually modifies or installs
new code into the SYS file code
or possibly uses non-standard or
"unusual" calls to ROM or DOS, I
would consider the upgrade well
worth the cost.

DISC LABELS:
Now for something completely
different.......

Book shops(such as Smiths ) sell
a self-adhesive film intended as
a protective covering for books.
It makes an ideal cover for disc
labels and has two purposes...

First,to protect frequently-used
discs (such as my W.P.) from
becoming dirty and worn from
handling.

Secondly, on clean new discs to
provide a writing surface that
can be used over and over again
- ideal for temporary files and
developing programs (and sending
things to OUTLET!).

I find for very short-term
writing the "Smiths Planner Pen"
is ideal and can be removed with
a very slightly damp cloth.

For more permanent use the
"overhead projector marker" is
better. This comes in a pack of
4 colours and each has its own
eraser.

If a lot of wording has to be
removed I find a cloth moistened
with methilated spirit is better
as I wouldn't recommend a lot of
"scrubbing"on the disc with the
eraser.

Other felt pens or markers may
be O.K. but try them out on a
scrap of film first.

The film is in various colours
but clear, I think, is best for
writing on.

          Malcolm Perry



Many thanks, Malcolm.  - Brian

From: Gerhard Behr, LANCASHIRE

Dear Brian,

Thank you very much for your
advice on my DUMP problem, which
as always was most helpful and
instructive. (OUTLET 44.1.43).

I did what you said: LOADed
"body of rev",pressed ESC,LOADed
my graphic, typed DUMP and lo
and behold!, it worked. So I
SAVEd your dumpld on my disk but
again nothing happened. I SAVEd
dumpld from the original SAMDOS
2 disk, again nothing. Then I
tried COPY and it worked! What
is wrong woth SAVE? I used the
proper CODE given by DIR 1 and
FSTAT gives identical results
for the COPYed and SAVEd file.

Your POKE also works well. I
have to use POKE 23068,18 to get
a proper circle. It makes it a
bit stripey, as you said, but
the result is not too bad.
                 - Gerhard Behr

The DUMP code is auto-run - that
is, it automatically runs when
it is loaded - like an auto-run
BASIC program. It does not do a
DUMP immediately, of course, but
"installs" itself - probably by
setting some system variables to
tell the SAM it's available and
moving to the highest free page
in memory. It changes itself on
the way or perhaps does not even
bother to move the bit of code
that does all this so SAVE will
only save this modified code and
not the original.     - Brian.

Another hardware project was a combined "switchable" joystick port and external key-board port.This was based on Adrian Dickens' designs in his excellent Manual 'Spectrum Hardware'. It differs from the standard stick by having 10 conductors in the

```text
             48K     128K
```

No press    0      224 Right       1      225

```text

  Down        4      228
  Up          8      232
  Fire       16      240
```

I suspect commercial software which does not insist on 48K mode must allow for differing inputs. Re: David Smith (Wolverhampton) Query: DATEL DOS.

Firstly I must stress I do not know what DOS DATEL are sending out with their +Ds since taking over from MGT therefore these notes are based on pre-DATEL information. Secondly, unless DATEL have altered things, 3C is more related to the DISCIPLE. So, bearing this uncertainty in mind, here goes.

Disciple started life,I believe, with a V2 ROM and associated DOS and was upgraded to V3 ROM and 3a DOS(review #1 Format AUG.87)

V3a dos was then progressivly upgraded to B,C then to D Each change was to overcome various bugs or problems that were found from use. (in fact c to d was,it seems, more to add in something that got left out of the C update). Without going into detail the latest version is more reliable with twin drives and handling OPENTYPE files. There was also a mod to prevent a hangup associated with BOOT if printer not on, A 128 mod to stop dropping back to 48k after a file COPY and so on.

The +D has 2 ROM versions 1 and 1A.The latter overcomes problems of some drives not finding track 0.(I believe). Therefore GDOS1 was changed to GDOS2 for ROM1a.

However, the two DOS's are basically the same. Both these were updated to 1a/2a again to overcome problems with OPENTYPE files, to work with the full screen editor in 128k mode and to prevent dropping back to 48k after a SAVE TO.

There were some v3 +D dos's (I had one) which I understand was a part conversion similar to the 'a update but not exactly the same (and caused me problems).

Is it worth upgrading? The obvi- ous answer is yes for the added reliability, removal of bugs and some snags. Also, I have found some programs will only work on the latest version of DOS.(Some state this).

There again, if you have not experienced any problems in the past then probably it's not worth spending to get the later version. The updates do not actually provide extended functions or facilities unless you update to UNI-DOS or BETADOS which is another matter.

Assuming DATEL have not altered things then 2A is the latest for the +D which D. Smith has.

For those interested,the follow- ing FORMATs cover the updates (the code to D.I.Y.) Disciple, #3 (a-b) #10(b-c) #11(c-d) +D #11 (1/2 to 1a/2a). Format also sell both the latest DOS (to members).

UNI-DOS update. (Disciple / +D) Since my review (OUTLET 45), I have used quite a lot more programs and sub routines mostly from various OUTLETS all without problems(The KEYWORD incompati- bility was covered in review and resolved). I consider the compatibility is a lot better than I first thought with GDOS. The colour dump problem has also been resolved with a small mod to the code. (This mod actually appeared in FORMAT V3 #3 for a different purpose and was to make the dump compatible with interfaces other than Disciple). I am certainly happy and the advantages outweigh the few disadvantages.I have also since found the author of Uni-Dos to be helpful.

Time has only strengthened my opinions in favour. Therefore, providing one is prepared to accept some incompatibilities mainly where the program actually modifies or installs new code into the SYS file code or possibly uses non-standard or "unusual" calls to ROM or DOS, I would consider the upgrade well worth the cost.

DISC LABELS: Now for something completely different.......

Book shops(such as Smiths ) sell a self-adhesive film intended as a protective covering for books. It makes an ideal cover for disc labels and has two purposes...

First,to protect frequently-used discs (such as my W.P.) from becoming dirty and worn from handling.

Secondly, on clean new discs to provide a writing surface that can be used over and over again - ideal for temporary files and developing programs (and sending things to OUTLET!).

For more permanent use the "overhead projector marker" is better. This comes in a pack of 4 colours and each has its own eraser.

Other felt pens or markers may be O.K. but try them out on a scrap of film first.

Когда появился 128K, переключатель был модифицирован, чтобы действовать как блок «Выбор компьютера», позволяющий использовать Datacorder с любым компьютером одним щелчком переключателя — и он до сих пор используется в таком виде.

Первоначально плата питалась от батареи PP9, но так как я часто забывал ее выключать, позже я подключил 9-вольтовый нестабилизированный выход от блока питания Sinclair, который затем питал плату через регулятор, который я добавил перед переходом на 128K.

Не вдаваясь в подробности, последняя версия надежнее работает с двумя дисководами и корректнее обрабатывает файлы OPENTYPE. Также был добавлен фикс, предотвращающий зависание при BOOT, если принтер выключен, патч для 128K, устраняющий сброс в режим 48K после COPY файла, и тому подобное.

У интерфейса +D есть две версии ПЗУ: 1 и 1A. Последняя исправляет проблемы некоторых дисководов, которые не могли найти нулевую дорожку (насколько мне известно). В связи с этим GDOS1 была изменена на GDOS2 для ПЗУ 1a.

Тем не менее, обе DOS практически идентичны. Они обе были обновлены до 1a/2a — опять же для устранения проблем с файлами OPENTYPE, для корректной работы с полноэкранным редактором в режиме 128K и предотвращения сброса в 48K после SAVE TO.

Существовали и некоторые версии v3 +D DOS (одна такая была у меня); насколько я понимаю, это была частичная конверсия, похожая на апдейт 'a', но не полностью аналогичная (и она доставляла мне проблемы).

Стоит ли обновляться? Очевидный ответ — да, ради повышенной надежности, исправления ошибок и мелких шероховатостей. Кроме того, я выяснил, что некоторые программы работают только на последней версии DOS (в некоторых это прямо указано).

С другой стороны, если у вас раньше не возникало никаких проблем, то, возможно, и не стоит тратить деньги на новую версию. Обновления не добавляют расширенных функций или возможностей, если только вы не переходите на UNI-DOS или BETADOS — но это уже совсем другая история.

Если DATEL ничего не меняли, то для +D, который есть у D. Smith, последней версией является 2A.

Для заинтересованных: следующие выпуски журнала FORMAT подробно описывают процесс обновления (коды для сборки своими руками): Disciple — #3 (a-b), #10 (b-c), #11 (c-d); +D — #11 (с 1/2 до 1a/2a). Журнал Format также продает обе последние версии DOS (членам клуба).

Апдейт по UNI-DOS (Disciple / +D).

Я считаю, что совместимость гораздо выше, чем мне первоначально казалось при сравнении с GDOS. Проблема со снятием цветного дампа экрана также решилась небольшой модификацией кода (эта модификация изначально появилась в FORMAT V3 #3 для другой цели — сделать дамп совместимым с интерфейсами помимо Disciple). Я определенно доволен, и преимущества перевешивают те немногие недостатки. К тому же автор Uni-Dos оказался весьма отзывчивым человеком.

Время лишь укрепило моё положительное мнение. Поэтому, если вы готовы смириться с некоторыми несовместимостями — в основном там, где программа модифицирует или внедряет новый код прямо в файл SYS, либо использует нестандартные или «необычные» вызовы ROM или DOS — я считаю, что этот апгрейд вполне стоит своих денег.

### ДИСКОВЫЕ ЭТИКЕТКИ:
А теперь нечто совершенно иное...

В книжных магазинах (например, Smiths) продаётся самоклеящаяся плёнка, предназначенная для защиты книжных обложек. Она идеально подходит для покрытия дисковых этикеток и служит двум целям...

Во-первых, защищает часто используемые диски (например, мой текстовый процессор) от грязи и засаливания при постоянном использовании.

Во-вторых, на чистых новых дисках она создаёт поверхность для записей, которую можно использовать снова и снова — идеальный вариант для временных файлов, разработки программ (и для отправки материалов в OUTLET!).

Я обнаружил, что для самых краткосрочных пометок отлично подходит «Smiths Planner Pen», который легко стирается едва влажной тряпочкой.

Для более долговечных надписей лучше использовать маркеры для проекторов («overhead projector marker»). Они продаются в наборе из четырёх цветов, и к каждому прилагается свой ластик.

Если нужно стереть много текста, я рекомендую тряпочку, смоченную техническим спиртом (метилатом), так как я бы не советовал усердно «тереть» диск ластиком.

Другие фломастеры или маркеры тоже могут подойти, но сначала проверьте их на отдельном кусочке плёнки.

Плёнка бывает разных цветов, но прозрачная, по-моему, лучше всего подходит для надписей.
